newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to reproduce the Shelby Cobra.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to reproduce the Shelby Cobra.

text.p: The Shelby Cobra, and other classic American sports car of the 1960s, will be reproduced in Malaysia beginning next year, Malaysia's national Bernama news agency reported over the weekend.

United Shelby Sdn Bhd, a Malaysian-Japanese-American company, plans to invest 338 million ringgit ($134 million) to revive Shelby cars, which ceased production in 1969, said Mohamed Fisol Ismail, chief executive of the joint-venture.
There are a limited number of original Shelbys in the world, and demand from enthusiasts is high, Fisol was quoted as saying by Bernama in Saturday's report.
He said the company hoped to begin exporting five Shelby models -- the Cobra, Daytona Cobra, GT40, GTSV8 and GTSV12 -- to the United States, Japan and Europe beginning in 1998.
"Our research in the United States shows that the demand for the Shelby Cobra exceeds supply, and waiting period for a Cobra can be as long as one year," he said.
The reproduction cars will be priced between $90,000 and $100,000, Fisol said.
He said the joint-venture firm will be 51 percent owned by Malaysians and the balance by individual foreign partners.
